# Gym recharge-time tuning sliders

## Goal

Gym-only live sliders to tune the Phase Shift / Teleport recharge times (like the existing spawn-interval slider pattern in `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts`), for balance observation in the gyms.

Recorded as out-of-scope during planning of AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR (Teleport and Phase Shift should recharge) — the recharge ACs use the level-derived defaults; tunable gym sliders are a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- (To be refined at intake) A gym control adjusts phase/teleport recharge times live and persists via the rules config.

Parent: **Performance testing skill — 50-enemy FPS sweep with a full random loadout** (AH-0MW3MGY3Z003R1M6).

## Goal

As an implementer I want the sweep planner's behaviour pinned by **failing** unit
tests before the implementation exists, so the implementation child is driven by
explicit expectations (step list, stop rule, seeded loadout, seeded shoot/dive
mix, summary) rather than by whatever the code happens to do.

This is the test-first slice of parent AC6 (seeded, reproducible loadout and mix)
and AC4 (stop rule / ceiling / budget).

## What to build (tests + a typed skeleton only)

1. `src/perf/sweepPlan.ts` — **exported types, constants and function
   signatures only**; every body is `throw new Error('not implemented')` so
   `npm run typecheck` stays clean while the specs fail red. Types:
   `SweepStepPlan`, `SweepLoadout`, `SweepWeaponGrant`, `SweepPowerUpGrant`,
   `SweepEnemyMix`, `SweepStepResult`, `SweepSummary`, `SweepStopReason`.
2. `src/perf/sweepPlan.test.ts` — fast unit specs (no Phaser, no browser) pinning:
   - **step list**: starts at 50, increments by 50, stops at the ceiling, and is
     truncated *before* the total-run budget would be exceeded;
   - **stop rule**: the first step whose average FPS is below 30 is the failure
     point, the previous step is the last playable load, and the ceiling/budget
     stops carry their own reason;
   - **loadout**: same seed → identical weapon/power-up sequence; at least one
     weapon from each broad category; at least one power-up; at most
     `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (6) counted kinds; levels non-maxed and monotone in the
     configured aggression;
   - **mix**: same seed → identical mix; every archetype is one of
     `GYM_PERFORMANCE_ARCHETYPE_KEYS`; counts sum to the step count; the diving
     proportion varies across steps;
   - **summary**: the per-step table row fields and the headline sentence.

## Key Files

- `src/perf/sweepPlan.ts` (new skeleton)
- `src/perf/sweepPlan.test.ts` (new spec)

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/perf/sweepPlan.test.ts` exists and every new spec fails for the
  documented not-implemented reason (no spec passes vacuously).
- `npm run typecheck` is clean — the skeleton is fully typed, no `any` escape.
- The specs cover the whole planner contract listed above, including the seeded
  determinism AC (parent AC6) and the stop rule / ceiling / budget AC (parent
  AC4).
- The specs land in the fast **unit** project: neither the module nor the spec
  imports `phaser` (import `hexAggressionLevel` from
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts`, not `deploymentLevelForAggression` from
  the scene module, so the import graph stays Phaser-free).
- No production behaviour changes: nothing imports the new module yet.
- The step planner, stop rule and summary are covered by fast unit tests
  (no browser) and `npm run typecheck` is clean; the scene-side half of the
  same parent AC (parameterised enemy count, loadout and mix seams covered
  by scene tests) is delivered by the sibling scene-test item.
data.title: Sweep planner contract tests (red)

data.description:
Parent: **Performance testing skill — 50-enemy FPS sweep with a full random loadout** (AH-0MW3MGY3Z003R1M6).

## Goal

Parent AC3 requires every sweep step to record **min, max and average FPS**, but
the shared harness report (`scripts/perf-report.mjs`) only exposes
`frameTimeMs.p50/p95/max/mean`, `fps.effective` and `fps.phaserActualFps` — there
is no minimum frame time, so the maximum FPS of a window is not recoverable from
the report.

As the producer I want the harness report to state min, max and average FPS
directly, so the sweep never re-derives them from a partial record.

## What to build

Extend the pure maths in `scripts/perf-report.mjs` (test-first):

- add `frameTimeMs.min` alongside the existing percentiles/max/mean;
- add `fps.min`, `fps.max` and `fps.mean` derived as `1000 / frameTimeMs.max`,
  `1000 / frameTimeMs.min` and `frames / elapsedSeconds` (the existing
  `fps.effective` stays, so no consumer breaks);
- keep the human summary and comparison formatting working (add the new figures
  where they clarify, never replacing existing lines);
- cover the new fields in `scripts/perf-report.test.ts` (empty window, single
  frame, a window with one long frame → min FPS is that frame's rate).

## Key Files

- `scripts/perf-report.mjs`
- `scripts/perf-report.test.ts`
- `scripts/measure-performance.mjs` (only if the summary needs the new fields)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A report built from known frame times carries `frameTimeMs.min` and
  `fps.min`, `fps.max`, `fps.mean`; the values equal the expected rates
  (e.g. a 50 ms frame gives `fps.min === 20`).
- Existing report fields (`frameTimeMs.p50/p95/max/mean`, `fps.effective`,
  `fps.phaserActualFps`, long-frame counts) are unchanged in name and meaning, so
  stored baselines stay comparable.
- `scripts/perf-report.test.ts` covers the new fields including the
  single-frame and empty-window edge cases.
- No browser is needed: the whole change is exercised by the existing fast unit
  tests.
data.title: Perf report min and max FPS
